item.title: Tottori Wagyu Beef: The Original Champion Bloodline — Guide
item.description: Tottori has an outsized place in the story of Japanese beef: the prefecture’s cattle descend in large part from a legendary stud bull, Ketaka-go, whose bloodline was so prized that it underpins many of Japan’s most famous wagyu brands elsewhere. Yet Tottori beef is far less known than the names it helped create, which makes it something of an insider’s choice. The local wagyu is specifically prized for its high oleic-acid content — a fat that melts at low temperature and gives a clean, sweet richness — and is served in the city and at farms as steak, sukiyaki, shabu-shabu and yakiniku, often at gentler prices than the headline brands.
